title: Karṇatantravajrapada (the Vajra Verses of the Whispered Lineage)
title_original: snyan brgyud rdo rje'i tshig rkang (Skt. title in the Tengyur: Karṇatantravajrapada)
alt_titles: Vajra Verses of the Hearing Lineage
snyan brgyud rdo rje'i tshig rkang

attribution.tradition: spoken by Vajradhara to the wisdom ḍākinī and transmitted in the hearing lineage of Tilopa and Nāropa; translated by Nāropa and Marpa at Puṣpahari (colophon)
attribution.scholarly: an Indian or Indo-Tibetan synopsis of the Nāropa system, 11th c.; catalogue author ascriptions not checked here

structure.description: c. 27 lines of the Derge folio (302b.6–304b.4), verse

summary: A compact verse synopsis of the whole hearing-lineage (snyan brgyud) path spoken in the voice of Vajradhara to the wisdom ḍākinī: the qualities of guru and disciple, the Cakrasaṃvara and Vajravārāhī empowerments, inner heat, illusory body, dream, clear light, transference and 'entering another's body', the consort practice (summarized here only), Mahāmudrā with an etymology of phyag rgya chen po, the three intermediate states with the dissolution at death, removal of obstacles by yantra exercises, and the fruit of Vajradhara in this life.

editions.name: Derge Tengyur, Tōh 2338 (read locally; Esukhia/Barom digital edition)

notes: Tōh 2338. Read in full locally. Passages on the consort practice and the yantra exercises are summarized only (restricted).

title: bka' dpe phyi ma (Nāropa's instructions received from Tilopa)
alt_titles: The Later Book of Instructions (tentative rendering)

attribution.tradition: Nāropa's instructions from Tilopa (the text's opening)
attribution.scholarly: Indian or early Tibetan compilation of the Nāropa instructions; author as given in catalogues not checked here

structure.description: c. 46 Derge lines (273a.4–276a.7); each section ends with a 'concise word' (tshig sbram) naming the kind of awakening it gives

summary: Nāropa's record of the instructions he received from Tilopa after reciting the Cakrasaṃvara mantra a hundred thousand times: the natural state of body and mind, the key points of body, time, object and wind; inner heat with its signs and warnings; illusory body; dream (four points); clear light (five kinds, five times); the kinds of transference with the warning that transference at the wrong time 'kills the deities'; the intermediate state with the stages of dissolution and the learner's and non-learner's union; 'entering another's body'; the method path; the rule of secrecy (the lioness's milk in an unfit vessel).

editions.name: Derge Tengyur, Tōh 2332 (read locally; Esukhia/Barom digital edition)

notes: Tōh 2332. Title rendering tentative; the text calls itself sealed three times (bka' rgya lan gsum).

title: Ājñāsamyakpramāṇa-nāma-ḍākinyupadeśa (the ḍākinī instruction 'True Measure of the Word')
title_original: bka' yang dag pa'i tshad ma zhes bya ba mkha' 'gro ma'i man ngag

attribution.tradition: a ḍākinī instruction; ascribed to Tilopa in the catalogues (from memory)

summary: A ḍākinī instruction that opens with the distinction between gradual and simultaneous persons ('the great medicine of the gradual is great poison for the simultaneous, and vice versa') and then outlines the path: taming afflictions, generation stage, speech isolation and wind, the great-bliss and Mahāmudrā instructions, inner heat and clear light, the illusory body, transference, dream (five points) and the intermediate state.

editions.name: Derge Tengyur, Tōh 2331 (read locally; Esukhia/Barom digital edition)

notes: Tōh 2331. The ascription to Tilopa is from memory of the catalogue and is not stated in the text read.

title: Dṛṣṭisaṃkṣipta (Nāropa's 'View in Brief')

attribution.tradition: Nāropa's (colophon: rje na ro pa'i lta ba mdor bsdus pa); translated and revised by Marpa

summary: Nāropa's short treatise on the view: conventionally all phenomena are nothing but self-aware mind; ultimately that mind is beyond existence and non-existence; appearance and emptiness are inseparable like a moon in water; mind is luminous and non-conceptual wisdom obscured by adventitious stains; its many names (bodhicitta, sugatagarbha, great bliss, secret mantra, great Madhyamaka, the fourth empowerment…) all refer to it; a correct view makes meditation and conduct reach the fruit.

editions.name: Derge Tengyur, Tōh 2304 (read locally; Esukhia/Barom digital edition)

title: Acintyamahāmudrā (Tilopa's 'Inconceivable' instructions)
title_original: phyag rgya chen po bsam gyis mi khyab pa

attribution.tradition: each section's colophon names Tilopa ('the lord of yogins Tillipa') as the instructor

structure.description: c. 109 Derge lines (245b.3–253a.5), several sections with their own colophons

summary: A cycle of Tilopa's instructions given to different people (a yogin in a royal city, a sorcerer, a singer, a courtesan and others), each called 'inconceivable': the unborn luminous dharmatā is the path of Mahāmudrā, free of identification and mentation; mind-itself is self-arisen wisdom; rest undistracted in the uncontrived mind; seeing it directly is the guru's kindness.

editions.name: Derge Tengyur, Tōh 2305 (read locally; Esukhia/Barom digital edition)

notes: Tōh 2305. Only the first sections were read in detail.

title: Śrīcakrasaṃvaropadeśa-mukhakarṇaparamparā-cintāmaṇi (the Wish-fulfilling Jewel of the Cakrasaṃvara whispered lineage)
title_original: dpal 'khor lo sdom pa'i man ngag zhal nas snyan du brgyud pa yid bzhin nor bu
summary: The ḍākinīs' secret words on the Cakrasaṃvara completion practices, 'arranged by Tilopa' (colophon), translated by Nāropa and Marpa at Puṣpahari; a root of the Kagyu hearing lineage.

editions.name: Derge Tengyur, Tōh 2337 (read locally; Esukhia/Barom digital edition)

notes: Tōh 2337. Only the opening and colophon were read.

title: The Six Yogas (Six Dharmas) of Nāropa

attribution.tradition: Tilopa's four transmissions (bka' babs bzhi), given to Nāropa and by him to Marpa
attribution.scholarly: the Indian roots are Tōh 2330 (Tilopa's Ṣaḍdharmopadeśa), 2331, 2332 and 2338; the list of six varies between sources

structure.description: not a single text: a cycle of root verses and Tibetan manuals

summary: The body of instructions on inner heat (gtum mo), illusory body (sgyu lus), dream (rmi lam), clear light ('od gsal), the intermediate state (bar do) and transference ('pho ba) — with 'entering another's body' (grong 'jug) and the consort practice in some lists — that Tilopa gathered from four Indian lineages and Nāropa passed to Marpa; the Kagyu 'path of method', on which every Kagyu school has its manuals (Gampopa, Phagmodrupa, Rangjung Dorje, Pema Karpo, Tsongkhapa's Gelug commentary).
notes: The practices are restricted: this ontology records summaries and the texts' warnings only.

title: The Hundred Thousand Songs of Milarepa
alt_titles: rje btsun mi la ras pa'i rnam thar rgyas par phye pa mgur 'bum

attribution.tradition: the songs are Milarepa's own; Tsangnyön Heruka gathered them
attribution.scholarly: compiled and substantially edited by Tsangnyön Heruka from earlier song collections; printed 1488

structure.description: c. 61 stories in three parts in the usual division (Chang's translation)

summary: The collected songs (mgur) of Milarepa set in narrative episodes — encounters with demons, disciples, patrons, rivals and his own practice in the caves of Lapchi, Chubar, Kailash and elsewhere — compiled and edited by Tsangnyön Heruka; the classic expression of Kagyu renunciation, inner heat and Mahāmudrā view.

editions.name: G. C. C. Chang, The Hundred Thousand Songs of Milarepa (1962)
Christopher Stagg, The Hundred Thousand Songs of Milarepa (2016)

title: The Jewel Ornament of Liberation
title_original: dam chos yid bzhin gyi nor bu thar pa rin po che'i rgyan

structure.description: 21 chapters in the usual division (chapter numbers used here follow it; verify)

summary: Gampopa's graded-path treatise, organized under six headings: the cause (buddha-nature), the basis (the precious human life), the condition (the spiritual friend), the method (the spiritual friend's instructions — impermanence, the suffering of saṃsāra, karma, love and compassion, refuge, bodhicitta and its trainings, the six perfections, the five paths and ten grounds), the result (the kāyas of buddhahood) and the activity (the Buddha's non-conceptual benefit of beings).

editions.name: H. V. Guenther, The Jewel Ornament of Liberation (1959)
Khenpo Konchog Gyaltsen, The Jewel Ornament of Liberation (1998)

title: Moonbeams of Mahāmudrā
title_original: nges don phyag rgya chen po'i sgom rim gsal bar byed pa'i legs bshad zla ba'i 'od zer

structure.description: two books: a general part (śamatha and vipaśyanā) and the special Mahāmudrā part; refs here are 'pt.1' / 'pt.2' only

summary: Dakpo Tashi Namgyal's great Mahāmudrā manual: a general presentation of śamatha and vipaśyanā common to sūtra and tantra, then the special Mahāmudrā — preliminaries, śamatha with and without support, vipaśyanā by examining the mind in stillness and movement, recognition, the deviations and strayings, the four yogas with their subdivisions and their relation to the paths and grounds, and the fruition.

editions.name: Lobsang P. Lhalungpa, Mahāmudrā: The Quintessence of Mind and Meditation (1986); Elizabeth Callahan, Moonbeams of Mahāmudrā (2019)

title: The Life of Milarepa
title_original: rnal 'byor gyi dbang phyug chen po mi la ras pa'i rnam thar thar pa dang thams cad mkhyen pa'i lam ston

structure.description: two parts ('black' and 'white' deeds), usually 12 chapters; refs here are 'pt.1', 'pt.2/n'

summary: Tsangnyön Heruka's biography of Milarepa in two parts: the 'black deeds' (the family's dispossession, sorcery and hail in revenge) and the 'white deeds' (Marpa's ordeals of tower-building, empowerment, solitary practice, disciples and death), framed as told to Rechungpa; the model of attaining buddhahood in one life through renunciation, devotion and effort.

editions.name: W. Y. Evans-Wentz / Kazi Dawa Samdup, Tibet's Great Yogī Milarepa (1928); Lobsang Lhalungpa, The Life of Milarepa (1977); Andrew Quintman, The Life of Milarepa (2010)

title: The Life of Marpa the Translator
title_original: sgra bsgyur mar pa lo tsa'i rnam par thar pa
summary: Tsangnyön Heruka's biography of Marpa: his journeys to India, study under Nāropa, Maitrīpa and others, his songs, his family and disciples, and the prophecies about his lineage.

editions.name: Nālandā Translation Committee, The Life of Marpa the Translator (1982)

title: The Life of Nāropa (by Lhatsün Rinchen Namgyal)
title_original: mkhas grub kun gyi gtsug rgyan paN chen nA ro pa'i rnam thar (title from memory)
summary: A Tibetan life of Nāropa: the ḍākinī's question at Nālandā, his search for Tilopa and the twelve great and twelve lesser hardships, and the instructions he received.

editions.name: H. V. Guenther, The Life and Teaching of Nāropa (1963)

notes: Tibetan title from memory; low confidence on its exact form.

title: The life and songs of Drukpa Kunley
summary: Accounts and songs of the Drukpa 'divine madman' Kunga Legpa: satire of religious hypocrisy and unconventional conduct read as teaching.
notes: Several compilations exist; the popular English version (Dowman, The Divine Madman) follows a later oral-literary compilation. Title left generic.

title: The Precious Garland of the Supreme Path
title_original: lam mchog rin po che'i phreng ba
summary: Gampopa's collection of practical precepts arranged in lists (mostly of ten): the causes of regret, the things to be done and avoided, the errors and the things not to be mistaken, the signs of the superior person, the great mistakes and the indispensables.

editions.name: W. Y. Evans-Wentz / Kazi Dawa Samdup, in Tibetan Yoga and Secret Doctrines (1935), Book I

notes: The exact number of chapters/lists (about 28) is from memory.

title: The Four Dharmas of Gampopa
summary: Gampopa's four-line summary of the whole path, recited as a supplication: grant blessings that the mind turn to the Dharma, that the Dharma become the path, that the path clarify confusion, and that confusion dawn as wisdom.

title: The Collected Works of Gampopa
summary: Gampopa's collected teachings: assembly teachings (tshogs chos), answers to the questions of his disciples (Düsum Khyenpa, Phagmodrupa, Gomtsul and others), instructions on co-emergent union and ordinary mind, and works on the graded path.
notes: Locators for passages cited from it are not known here; teachings use topic anchors.

title: The Profound Inner Meaning

structure.description: chapters on mind, the formation of the body, channels, winds, drops, death and the path (the exact chapter count, c. 11, is not certain)

summary: The 3rd Karmapa's treatise on the vajra body and the ground of tantra: how mind, confused, forms the body with its channels, winds and drops, the correspondence of body and cosmos, the dying process, and how the completion-stage practices purify them; with his autocommentary.

title: The Aspiration Prayer of Mahāmudrā
title_original: nges don phyag rgya chen po'i smon lam

structure.description: about 25 verses (numbering varies by edition; teachings use section anchors)

summary: The 3rd Karmapa's verse prayer of the definitive meaning: aspirations for hearing, reflection and meditation; the ground, path and fruit of purification; the view of mind neither existent nor non-existent; appearances as mind and mind as empty; śamatha and vipaśyanā; the four yogas; and the union of emptiness and compassion.

editions.name: many (e.g. in Thrangu Rinpoche's and Tai Situ Rinpoche's commentaries)

title: Distinguishing Consciousness and Wisdom
summary: The 3rd Karmapa's short treatise distinguishing the eight consciousnesses (rnam shes) from the wisdoms (ye shes) they become when their nature is recognized.

title: Treatise on Buddha-Nature (the 3rd Karmapa)
title_original: de bzhin gshegs pa'i snying po bstan pa
summary: The 3rd Karmapa's verse treatise on buddha-nature, opening from the Mahāyānābhidharma sūtra's verse on the beginningless element: mind's nature, luminous clarity-emptiness, is buddha-nature, obscured by adventitious stains and revealed by the path.

title: The Chariot of the Dakpo Kagyu Siddhas
title_original: dbu ma la 'jug pa'i rnam bshad dpal ldan dus gsum mkhyen pa'i zhal lung dwags brgyud grub pa'i shing rta
summary: The 8th Karmapa's commentary on Candrakīrti's Madhyamakāvatāra, presenting the Kagyu reading of Prāsaṅgika Madhyamaka (and criticizing positions of other schools).

title: The Four-Session Guru Yoga
summary: The 8th Karmapa's guru yoga, practised in four sessions a day, supplicating the Karmapa as the embodiment of all lineage gurus and receiving the four empowerments.

title: The Ocean of Kagyu Songs (The Rain of Wisdom)
summary: An anthology of vajra songs (mgur) of the Kagyu masters from Vajradhara and Tilopa through the Karmapas, compiled under the 8th Karmapa.

editions.name: Nālandā Translation Committee, The Rain of Wisdom (1980)

title: Mahāmudrā: The Ocean of Definitive Meaning
title_original: phyag rgya chen po nges don rgya mtsho
summary: The 9th Karmapa's large Mahāmudrā manual: the common, uncommon and special preliminaries; śamatha; vipaśyanā; the pointing-out of mind; enhancement and removal of obstacles; the four yogas; the fruition.

editions.name: Elizabeth Callahan, Mahāmudrā: The Ocean of Definitive Meaning (2001)

title: Mahāmudrā: Eliminating the Darkness of Ignorance
title_original: phyag rgya chen po ma rig mun sel
summary: The 9th Karmapa's medium-length Mahāmudrā manual (the middle of his three), arranged as a sequence of meditation sessions.

title: Pointing Out the Dharmakāya
summary: The 9th Karmapa's short Mahāmudrā manual, the pointing-out instruction arranged for practice: preliminaries, śamatha, vipaśyanā, and the pointing-out of mind in stillness and movement, of appearances as mind, of mind as empty, and of emptiness as self-liberated.

editions.name: with Khenchen Thrangu's commentary, Pointing Out the Dharmakaya (2003)

title: A Feast for Scholars
summary: Pawo Tsuglag Trengwa's history of Buddhism in India and Tibet, with extensive Karma Kagyu history.

title: The Blue Annals
summary: Gö Lotsāwa Zhönu Pal's history of the Tibetan transmissions, with detailed Kagyu lineage histories; source for the report that Gampopa taught Mahāmudrā also apart from tantric initiation and for the Indian (Maitrīpa, Sahajavajra) precedent of Mahāmudrā joined with the pāramitā path.

editions.name: G. N. Roerich, The Blue Annals (1949–53)

title: Gö Lotsāwa's commentary on the Ratnagotravibhāga
title_original: theg pa chen po rgyud bla ma'i bstan bcos kyi 'grel bshad de kho na nyid rab tu gsal ba'i me long (title from memory)
summary: Gö Lotsāwa's explanation of the Ratnagotravibhāga as a basis of Mahāmudrā (the 'Mirror Illuminating Reality').

title: Clarifying the Natural State
title_original: phyag rgya chen po'i khrid yig (full title not certain)
summary: Dakpo Tashi Namgyal's concise guidance manual of Mahāmudrā (preliminaries, śamatha, vipaśyanā, the pointing-out and the four yogas), the practical counterpart of Moonbeams.

editions.name: Erik Pema Kunsang, Clarifying the Natural State (2001)

title: The Single Intent (Gongchig)
alt_titles: dam chos dgongs pa gcig pa
The Single Intent, the Sacred Dharma

structure.description: c. 150 vajra statements in seven chapters with a later supplement (counts from memory; verify)

summary: The Drikung collection of Jigten Sumgön's 'vajra statements' on the unity of the Buddha's teaching, compiled by his disciple Sherab Jungne, with later commentaries (Dorje Sherab's 'Light of the Sun' and others): all teachings share one intent; the three vows are one in essence.

title: The Ultimate Supreme Path of Mahāmudrā
title_original: phyag chen lam mchog mthar thug
summary: Lama Zhang's Mahāmudrā instruction: devotion and the guru's blessing as the door of realization, the nature of mind, meditation without fabrication, and the pitfalls on the way.
notes: Title from memory; content summary at low confidence.

title: The Six Cycles of Equal Taste
summary: A Drukpa cycle said to have been hidden by Rechungpa and rediscovered by Tsangpa Gyare: instructions for carrying thoughts, afflictions, gods and demons, suffering, illness and death onto the path as one taste.
notes: The list of six is from memory (low confidence).

title: The Treasury of the Victorious Ones (Pema Karpo's Mahāmudrā)
title_original: phyag rgya chen po'i man ngag gi bshad sbyar rgyal ba'i gan mdzod (title from memory)
summary: Pema Karpo's explanation of Mahāmudrā instruction, defending and systematizing the Kagyu view.

title: The Epitome of the Great Symbol (Pema Karpo)
summary: Pema Karpo's short Mahāmudrā manual: preliminaries, the ordinary practice (śamatha and vipaśyanā), the extraordinary practice, and the four yogas.

editions.name: Evans-Wentz / Kazi Dawa Samdup, Tibetan Yoga and Secret Doctrines (1935), Book II

title: The Epitome of the Six Doctrines (Pema Karpo)
title_original: chos drug bsdus pa'i zin bris
summary: Pema Karpo's summary manual of the Six Yogas of Nāropa.

editions.name: Evans-Wentz / Kazi Dawa Samdup, Tibetan Yoga and Secret Doctrines (1935), Book III

notes: Restricted content: this ontology records only summaries and warnings.

title: The Hidden Description of the Vajra Body
title_original: rdo rje lus kyi sbas bshad
summary: Yangönpa's treatise on the vajra body — the formation of channels, winds and drops in the womb and their role on the path.

title: The Lamp of Mahāmudrā
summary: Tselé Natsok Rangdröl's concise manual of Mahāmudrā view, meditation and conduct, drawing also on Dzogchen.

editions.name: Erik Pema Kunsang, Lamp of Mahamudra (1989)

title: The Union of Mahāmudrā and Dzogchen
summary: Karma Chagmé's instructions showing Mahāmudrā and Dzogchen as one in essence and practising them together.

editions.name: with Gyatrul Rinpoche's commentary, A Spacious Path to Freedom / Naked Awareness (1998–2000)

title: Mountain Dharma (Karma Chagmé)
title_original: ri chos mtshams kyi zhal gdams (title from memory)
summary: Karma Chagmé's retreat teachings (ri chos) for practitioners in strict retreat.

title: The Short Vajradhara Lineage Prayer (Dorje Chang Thungma)
summary: The most widely recited Kagyu supplication: it invokes the lineage from Vajradhara, Tilopa, Nāropa, Marpa, Milarepa and Gampopa, and states the path in four verses — revulsion is the feet of meditation, devotion its head, non-distraction its main body, and the nature of thought is dharmakāya.

title: The Vajra Lines of Niguma's Six Dharmas
title_original: ni gu chos drug gi rdo rje'i tshig rkang (title from memory)
summary: Niguma's root verses of the six dharmas — inner heat, illusory body, dream, clear light, transference and the intermediate state — each with the kind of self-liberation it brings.

editions.name: Sarah Harding, Niguma, Lady of Illusion (2010)

title: The Mahāmudrā of the Amulet Box
summary: Niguma's Mahāmudrā instruction: the ground, path and fruit 'enclosed together like the two halves of an amulet box'; the three self-liberations, the four faults self-liberated, and the four kāyas as fruition.

title: The Three Integrations (Shangpa)
summary: The Shangpa instruction on carrying the guru, the deity and illusion onto the path in all activities.

title: The White and Red Khecarī (Shangpa)
summary: The Shangpa practice cycle of the white and red sky-goers (Khecarī), the 'flowers' of the five golden dharmas.

title: The Deathless Body and Mind (Shangpa)
summary: The Shangpa cycle on the 'undying and unerring' mind and body, the fruit of the five golden dharmas.

title: The Six Dharmas of Sukhasiddhi
summary: Sukhasiddhi's instructions transmitted in the Shangpa, parallel to Niguma's six dharmas.

title: The Benefit of Beings Pervading Space (Thangtong Gyalpo's Avalokiteśvara practice)
summary: Thangtong Gyalpo's short Avalokiteśvara sādhana: refuge and bodhicitta, visualizing Avalokiteśvara above one's head, light purifying all beings, recitation of the six-syllable mantra, and resting with appearances, sounds and awareness as the deity's body, speech and mind.

title: Tilopa's Six Nails of Key Points (the six words of advice)
summary: Tilopa's six-word instruction to Nāropa on resting the mind: do not recall, do not imagine, do not think, do not examine, do not control, rest.
notes: The instruction is widely quoted in the Kagyu; the source text and its exact Tibetan wording were not found locally. U44 (Tilopa) may hold a parallel entry.

title: The Torch of Certainty
summary: Jamgön Kongtrul's commentary on the Kagyu (Mahāmudrā) preliminaries: the four thoughts that turn the mind and the four special preliminaries (refuge with prostrations and bodhicitta, Vajrasattva, maṇḍala offering, guru yoga).

editions.name: Judith Hanson, The Torch of Certainty (1977)

title: The Treasury of Kagyu Mantra
summary: Jamgön Kongtrul's collection of the empowerments and practices of the Marpa Kagyu tantric cycles.
